bug_semantics: A client able to change the X server font path can create a directory whose fonts.alias maps an alias to a 257-1023-byte target, add that directory with SetFontPath, and request the alias with ListFonts or ListFontsWithInfo. libXfont2 accepts and returns names/alias targets up to its 1024-byte MAXFONTNAMELEN, while the server historically used XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN=256 for the stack-local tmp_pattern and the LFWIstateRec current.pattern arrays. doListFontsAndAliases copied resolvedlen bytes into tmp_pattern and then current.pattern without checking resolvedlen; doListFontsWithInfo likewise copied namelen bytes into current.pattern without checking namelen. The oversized library-produced target therefore writes beyond stack buffers, permitting a server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server runs as root.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable 256-byte server buffers and all three relevant unchecked alias-resolution copies are already present in ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, the 2003-11-14 whole-tree snapshot whose message is 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'. That changeset creates dix/dixfonts.c and include/closestr.h wholesale on top of a parent containing neither path, so it is an aggregate import boundary rather than the smallest source commit and is rejected as the BIC. Later 05a793f5b3c40747d5a92a076def7f4fb673c7e7 merely migrated the pre-existing code from libXfont to libXfont2, and 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391 merely changed non-overlapping memmove calls to memcpy; neither first introduced the unchecked length-versus-buffer mismatch. The true originating source change predates the fine-grained history available for these paths in this repository.

For boundary diagnosis only, `git cat-file commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1` shows author and committer Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>, parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941, and only the one-line baseline message, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI marker. That non-BIC object is not used to classify AI involvement. The fix object's `Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-6` trailer is deliberately ignored because AI evidence is BIC-only.
evidence: First-party advisory https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html describes the 256-versus-1024 mismatch, the 257-1023-byte triggering range, stack overflow impact, and names bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 as the fix; it states that X.Org X server before 21.1.23 and Xwayland before 24.1.12 are affected and that those two releases contain the fixes.

In the assigned clone, `git show --format=fuller bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07` shows a direct two-file fix: dix/closestr.h raises XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN from 256 to 1024, dix/dixfonts.c checks resolvedlen before copying to tmp_pattern in doListFontsAndAliases, and checks namelen before copying to current.pattern in doListFontsWithInfo. Its sole parent is ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05.

`git grep -n -e 'memmove *(tmp_pattern' -e 'memmove *(c->current.pattern' ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- dix/dixfonts.c` reports unchecked copies at lines 668, 696, and 952. `git grep -n XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- include/closestr.h` reports the 256 definition at line 64 and pattern array at line 66. Thus the complete vulnerable sink structure exists at the earliest snapshot for these paths.

`git show -s --format='%H%n%P%n%B' ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1` gives parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 and message 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'. `git show --stat ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- dix/dixfonts.c include/closestr.h` shows both files created wholesale (2,266 inserted lines), while `git ls-tree -r --name-only cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 dix/dixfonts.c include/closestr.h` returns no paths. This directly verifies absence in the import parent's tree but does not satisfy introducer-parent absence because the import is not a valid smallest BIC.

`git blame -w bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07^ -L 650,705 -- dix/dixfonts.c`, `git blame -w ... -L 900,950`, and the corresponding closestr.h blame assign the buffer declaration, alias handling, and the still-memmove ListFontsWithInfo sink to ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1; only the spelling of two ListFonts copies points to 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391. `git show 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391 -- dix/dixfonts.c` confirms a semantics-preserving memmove-to-memcpy cleanup and explicitly says the operations largely came from a 1993 mass bcopy-to-memmove substitution, reinforcing that this 2022 commit is not the BIC.

`git show 05a793f5b3c40747d5a92a076def7f4fb673c7e7 -- configure.ac dix/dixfonts.c` shows the 2016 API migration changing the dependency from xfont >= 1.4.2 to xfont2 >= 2.0.0 and renaming/calling through the new API without adding the fixed 256-byte arrays or unchecked copies. The official libXfont 1.5.1 source at https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libxfont/-/raw/9fee60267329867b7a61eae39179b481ae89411e/include/X11/fonts/fntfilst.h already defines MAXFONTNAMELEN as 1024, and its dirfile.c uses MAXFONTNAMELEN-sized alias and target buffers, so the mismatch predates the libXfont2 migration.

Release boundary reproduction: `git grep -n XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN xorg-server-21.1.22 -- dix/dixfonts.c` shows tmp_pattern with no resolvedlen/namelen guards; the same command at xorg-server-21.1.23 shows new guards at lines 673 and 939. `git show xorg-server-21.1.22:include/closestr.h` has `#define XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN 256`, while xorg-server-21.1.23 has 1024. Equivalent guard absence/presence is visible between xwayland-24.1.11 and xwayland-24.1.12.

The release-branch commits are a569eb4f36ed96a9e445ececd7e8d98c223461a0 for xorg-server-21.1.23 and 93596a0b4dec958cc8f614fc25a2b68c8edc852a for xwayland-24.1.12. `git show -s` on each records `(cherry picked from commit bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07)`, and `git tag --contains` places the former first in xorg-server-21.1.23 and the latter first in xwayland-24.1.12. The advisory-referenced mainline commit remains the direct fix recorded in fix_sha/direct_fix_sha.

reasoning: The vulnerability is fully closed at the fix end: the attack-controlled alias target reaches three unchecked copies into 256-byte stack-resident buffers, the direct fix both aligns the server capacity with libXfont2 and adds defensive length checks, and the two release backports establish the stated fixed-version boundary. The origin end cannot be closed without violating the smallest-real-BIC rule. Git -S and blame lead to a 2003 R6.6 baseline import that creates the affected files wholesale, its direct parent lacks the paths entirely, and later candidate changes are demonstrably API or copy-primitive refactors over already-vulnerable logic. Because that aggregate snapshot is not an eligible BIC and cannot be decomposed into original source commits from this clone, there is no true BIC commit object from which to make the required AI-only judgment. The later Claude assistance on the fix is irrelevant. This is therefore a genuine history-boundary BLOCKED result, not NOT_AI and not an AI attribution.
remaining_gap: The repository needs commit-level pre-R6.6 history for the original introduction of the 256-byte XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN-backed alias buffers and unchecked alias-target copies (including the immediate parent), or a trustworthy mapping from the 2003 baseline snapshot to those original source commits. Without that history, the smallest BIC, its parent-absence proof, and the BIC commit object's AI marker status are unavailable; the aggregate ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 cannot substitute for them.
